s0183 introduces 合弟秉 and s0185-s0189 continue his career: 彭城王勰征壽春，秉從行. Bing is Cui Bing p106, the local subject of this biography, not the prince or Shouchun. Other Cui Bing records are not being merged.

s0198 秉堅守歷年...與秉第二子仲哲赴救 repeats the same defender as the father of Zhongzhe. p106 already owns the first Bing in this unit and the surrounding siege narrative. Link the second possessive Bing to p106, not commander Yuan Tan or the son.

s0202 除秉為刺史 names the appointee in the continuous Cui Bing biography after the siege. It refers to local p106, not the province or a new bearer of Bing. The time wording is read for narrative continuity only; no chronology is approved.
s0213 introduces 長子忻，字伯悅. In s0215 常景引為行臺郎...復為安遠將軍 the omitted object/continuing appointee is that same 忻, explicitly supplied as Xin in English. Link p111, not his recruiter Chang Jing p114.

s0219 introduces 仲哲 and s0224 及父秉於燕州被圍 identifies his father. This recalls s0198 秉第二子仲哲赴救 in p106's siege narrative. The father Bing is p106; the following Yuan Tan is the relief commander, not the father.
s0228 仲哲弟叔彥 explicitly names Zhongzhe as Shuyan's elder brother, continuing the Zhongzhe introduced at s0219 and named in s0225. The English possessive Zhongzhe links to p112, while Shuyan is p120.

s0246 秉從父弟廣 names Bing as Guang's older paternal cousin after the nearby 秉弟習 branch. In this local extraction branch, p126 owns 秉 at s0233/s0235/s0237 and is the endpoint of Guang p132's source-backed s0246 kinship claim c1073. Retain that local owner for the callback; this does not merge the duplicate-looking p106/p126/p161 records.

s0246 introduces 廣字仲慶. In s0250 引廣為鎮南府長史，以母老辭 the recruited Guang declines because of his mother. The second English Guang is the same p132 already linked to the first Guang in the sentence, not Prince Cheng p134.

s0274 identifies the name 系, and s0275 按本名「緯」 explicitly says his original name was Wei. This is the personal-name variant 緯 of the local Li Xi p148, already linked to 緯 in Chinese here, not the surname of Wei Shou or Li Xianfu's posthumous epithet.

s0276 作「偉」，是「緯」的形訛 compares the transmitted spelling of the same name discussed at s0274-s0275. The first English Wei represents the explicitly rejected written form 偉 of Li Xi/Wei p148's name. Link the discussed referent as a textual-name variant only; do not add a claim that 偉 was his true name or confuse this with Li Hun, whose biography is cited as the witness.

The second Wei in s0276 corresponds to 「緯」 in 是「緯」的形訛, the original name explicitly attributed to p148 in s0275. The English latitude gloss distinguishes the written character, but its referent remains the same discussed personal name. It is neither a geographical latitude mention nor the unrelated Wei epithet of p021.

s0279 quotes 陽平王頤 then compares the readings 頤/顯/順. This second Yi repeats the name 頤 of the quoted prince, already linked locally to p153; s0287 and s0289 explain why 頤 is retained. Link that discussed name, not Li Yi 翼, Prince Yi 懌, or Li Can's posthumous epithet. The alternative readings remain textually qualified and no identities are merged.

s0280 explicitly names 元顯; s0282 有元顯墓誌...顯所襲 refers again to that epitaph subject and his inherited title. The final English Xian is p154, already linked to Yuan Xian earlier in s0282, not Prince Yi or a place. No genealogy or dates are changed.

evidence.zh: 北道行臺常景引為行臺郎，又啟除員外郎，復為安遠將軍、尚書左中兵郎中。

evidence.literal: As nephew of Zheng Yan, he concurrently served as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 父勰，字小同，恬靜好學，有聲趙魏。
units.en: His father Xie, whose courtesy name was Xiaotong, was calm and studious and enjoyed renown across Zhao and Wei.
units.literal: His father Xie, styled Xiaotong, was quiet and fond of learning; he had a reputation in Zhao and Wei.

units.en: He's younger brother Bing was spirited and resolute even in youth.
units.literal: He's younger brother Bing, in youth had will and spirit.

units.zh: 陽平王頤之為定州，[4]秉復為衞軍府錄事參軍，帶毋極令。
units.en: When Prince of Yangping Yizhi served at Dingzhou, [4] Bing again became recording clerk of the guard army command, concurrently serving as magistrate of Wuji.
units.literal: When the Prince of Yangping Yizhi served at Dingzhou, [4] Bing again became recording clerk of the Guard Army command, concurrently magistrate of Wuji.

units.zh: 時甄琛為長史，因公事言競之間，秉以拳擊琛，墜於牀下。
units.en: Zhen Chen was then chief secretary; during a dispute over official business Bing punched him and knocked him off the bed.
units.literal: At that time Zhen Chen was chief secretary; during public business a verbal dispute arose between them, and Bing struck Chen with his fist and knocked him from the bed.

units.en: As magistrate of the county Chen only laughed and let the matter pass.
units.literal: Because Chen was magistrate of this county, he laughed and did not pursue the matter.

units.en: Such was his bold and unrestrained character.
units.literal: His bold forthrightness was like this.

units.zh: 彭城王勰征壽春，秉從行，招致壯俠，以為部卒。
units.en: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie campaigned against Shouchun, Bing accompanied him, recruited bold adventurers, and enrolled them as company soldiers.
units.literal: When the Prince of Pengcheng Xie campaigned against Shouchun, Bing followed on the expedition, recruited gallant bravos, and made them company soldiers.

units.zh: 勰目之，謂左右曰：「吾當寄膽氣於此人。」
units.en: Xie looked him over and told his attendants, "I mean to place my courage in this man's keeping."
units.literal: Xie fixed his gaze on him and said to those beside him: "I shall entrust my bold spirit to this man."

units.zh: 後為司空主簿，轉掾、城門校尉、長兼司空司馬。
units.en: He later served as chief clerk of the minister of works, then as secretary, commandant of the city gates, and senior staff member concurrently serving as grand marshal of the minister of works.
units.literal: Later he was made Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, transferred to secretary, Commandant of the City Gates, and senior concurrently Grand Marshal of the Minister of Works.

units.en: Bing's younger brother Xi, whose courtesy name was Guili, enjoyed inherited family repute.
units.literal: Bing's younger brother Xi, styled Guili, enjoyed inherited family repute.

units.zh: 歷司徒主簿、彭城王勰開府屬。
units.en: He served successively as chief clerk under the minister of works and on the opening office staff of Prince of Pengcheng Xie.
units.literal: He served successively as chief clerk under the Minister of Works and a member of Prince of Pengcheng Xie's opening office staff.

units.zh: 遷幽州長史、博陵太守，吏民愛敬之。
units.en: He was transferred to chief secretary of Youzhou and administrator of Bolling, where officials and commoners loved and respected him.
units.literal: He was transferred to chief secretary of Youzhou and Administrator of Bolling; officials and commoners loved and respected him.
